question: The star-shaped temples were built during the reign of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hoysala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The star-shaped temples,** emblematic of the **Hoysala Dynasty's **architectural prowess, emerged during the reign of** King Vishnuvardhana,** spanning from 1117 CE to over a century later.
 
• Notable for their distinctive star-shaped sanctum sanctorum, or Stellate plan, these temples showcase intricate designs and exquisite craftsmanship.
 
• Elaborate carvings, finely detailed sculptures, and decorative panels adorn both the interior and exterior walls of these remarkable structures.
 
• The Hoysalas established their unique architectural style, known as the Hoysala school of art, flourishing between 1050–1300 AD.
 
• Constructed primarily from soapstone, these temples stand as enduring testaments to the ingenuity and artistic legacy of the **Hoysala Dynasty.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Hoysala dynasty, **a prominent Kannadiga power, held sway over southern India from 1006 to 1346 CE.
 
• Initially headquartered in Belur, the capital later shifted to Halebidu.
 
• Renowned for their philanthropy, the Hoysalas left enduring legacies through the construction of tanks, temples, and patronage of educational institutions.
